title: Replication-Independent Generation and Morphological Analysis of Flavivirus Replication Organelles
protocol: Insert parts of the viral genome (ETm-3′ UTR) into the pTM expression plasmid.
Add an EMCV IRES element to the 5′ end of the viral open reading frame encoding the polyprotein.
Insert the hepatitis D virus ribozyme downstream of the ZIKV or DENV 3′ UTR.
Transfect the Huh7/Lunet-T7 cell line with the DNA plasmid containing the modified viral genome.
Continuously produce viral RNA in the transfected cells due to cytoplasmic transcription via the T7 RNA polymerase promoter.
Seed Huh7/Lunet-T7 cells for transfection experiments.
Seed Huh7/Lunet-T7 cells on glass coverslips in 24-well plates at a density of 3 × 10^4 cells/well one day prior to transfection.
Seed Huh7/Lunet-T7 cells in 6-well plates at a density of 2 × 10^5 cells/well one day prior to transfection.
Change the medium of seeded cells on the day of transfection, at least 30 minutes before transfection.
Replace the medium with 500 μL pre-warmed DMEM complete medium per well for 24-well plates.
Replace the medium with 1 mL pre-warmed DMEM complete medium per well for 6-well plates.
Place 100 μL OptiMEM reduced serum medium into a sterile reaction tube for 24-well plates.
Place 400 μL OptiMEM reduced serum medium into a sterile reaction tube for 6-well plates.
Add 500 ng plasmid DNA to the OptiMEM in the reaction tube for 24-well plates and gently vortex.
Add 2 μg plasmid DNA to the OptiMEM in the reaction tube for 6-well plates and gently vortex.
Add 1.5 μL Mirus TransIT-LT1 transfection reagent to the DNA mixture for 24-well plates, avoiding contact with the tube sides.
Add 6 μL Mirus TransIT-LT1 transfection reagent to the DNA mixture for 6-well plates, avoiding contact with the tube sides.
Mix the DNA and transfection reagent thoroughly by vortexing.
Incubate the mixture at approximately 22°C for 20 minutes.
Warm the transfection reagent to approximately 22°C and gently vortex before usage.
Scale up the transfection mixture accordingly if more than one well is being transfected.
Add the transfection mixtures to the cells drop-wise.
Gently rock the plates back-and-forth and side-to-side to ensure even distribution of the TransIT-LT1 reagent:DNA complexes.
Incubate the plates for 4 hours at 37°C in a 5% CO2 environment.
Change the transfection medium to fresh DMEM complete after incubation.
Allow expression of the polyprotein for a maximum of 18 hours (pIRO-Z) or 20 hours (pIRO-D).
Wash cells three times with sterile PBS prior to fixation.
Fix cells with 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS for 10 minutes at approximately 22°C.
Wash fixed cells three times with sterile PBS.
Store PFA-fixed cells at 4°C covered with 1 mL of PBS for up to one week.
Proceed directly with further processing or store electron microscopy samples in fixation buffer at 4°C for up to three days.
Add sufficient amount of fixative buffer to the well to keep the coverslips covered.
Cells are lysed by adding 100 μL/well of 2× sample buffer supplemented with 1 μL of benzonase (stock: 10KU).
Degradation of nucleic acids is allowed for 5 min at ∼22°C.
Transfer samples to 1.5 mL reaction tubes and heat samples at 95°C for 5 min.
Cells are permeabilized with 0.5 mL 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS for up to 10 min at ∼22°C.
Permeabilized cells are washed three times with 1 mL PBS before being incubated for 1 h in 0.5 mL blocking buffer (10% FCS in PBS) at ∼22°C.
Primary antibodies against ZIKV NS4B are diluted 1:250 in 3% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS.
Incubation with primary antibodies can either be done at 4°C for up to 16 h or 2 h at ∼22°C.
Coverslips are washed three times with PBS-T (0.01% Tween20) 10 min each.
Alexa Fluorophore 568-conjugated secondary antibodies are diluted 1:1,000 in 3% BSA in PBS.
Incubate cells with secondary antibodies for 1 hour at approximately 22°C in the dark.
Wash samples three times with PBS-T (0.01% Tween20) for 10 minutes each.
Rinse coverslips once with ddH2O before mounting.
Mount coverslips on microscopy slides using 5 μL of Fluoromount-G supplemented with DAPI to stain nuclear DNA.
Air dry samples for at least 30 minutes at approximately 22°C before analysis.
Record large overview pictures (5 × 5) using the 20× magnification objective.
Calculate transfection efficiency by determining the number of NS4B-positive cells over the total number of cells.
Set recording picture settings in the beginning and do not change them for other samples.
Subject 15 μL of protein sample to a 15% SDS-PAGE gel.
Perform electrophoresis for 2 hours at constant 100 V.
Transfer proteins onto a 0.45 μm PVDF membrane at 350 mA for 1 hour at 4°C using the wet blot transfer system of Bio-Rad.
Block membranes in 5% milk in PBS.
Dilute primary antibodies (ZIKV NS1, NS2B, NS3, and NS4A) to a ratio of 1:1,000 in 1% milk in PBS.
Incubate membranes at 4°C for up to 16 hours.
Wash membranes three times with PBS-T (0.1% Tween20), 10 minutes each.
Dilute HRP-conjugated secondary antibodies (anti-mouse and anti-rabbit) in 1% milk in PBS.
Incubate membranes for 1 hour at approximately 22°C.
Wash membranes three times with PBS-T (0.1% Tween20), 10 minutes each.
Develop Western blots using the Western Lightning Plus-ECL reagent.
Take images of Western blot using the ChemoStar imager software package.
Analyze Western blot images using the FIJI software package.
Rinse samples five times with 50 mM cacodylate buffer for 5 min each.
Incubate samples with 2% osmium tetroxide in 50 mM cacodylate buffer for at least 40 min on ice.
Wash samples three times with EM-grade water.
Incubate samples with 0.5% aqueous uranyl acetate at 4°C for up to 16 h.
Rinse samples three times with EM-grade water the next day.
Dehydrate samples using a graded ethanol series (from 50% to 100%).
Flip coverslips on epoxy resin filled capsules.
Polymerize Epon at 60°C for at least 48 h.
Trim polymerized sample to a 0.5 x 0.5 mm sized section using a razor blade.
Mount trimmed block into an ultramicrotome holder.
Align specimens’ surface with the diamond knife in all axis.
Clean the diamond knife with methanol before sectioning.
Fill the boat of the diamond knife with H2O up to the knife’s edge.
Cut 70 nm thin sections automatically by the microtome.
Pick up floating sections with a loop and transfer them onto a formvar-coated TEM grid.
Dry the grid by air at approximately 22°C.
Fix parafilm on a paper or table.
Transfer grids with sections to aqueous uranyl acetate (3%) droplets and incubate for 5 minutes.
Wash grids with ddH2O by transferring them onto droplets and leaving them for 30 seconds.
Repeat the washing step two times.
Transfer grids to aqueous lead citrate droplets and incubate for 5 minutes.
Wash grids following instructions in step iii.
Dry grids at approximately 22°C before analysis.
Analyze grids on a JEOL JEM-1400 transmission electron microscope.
